verdict.line: You lose if you trade into a live E (Apprehend) before level 6; you win if you parry that pull with W or stall to your item spike around level 9-11.

brief.thesis: Darius holds lane advantage and the solo-kill edge (47.7% Fiora win rate over 486 games) because his entire all-in depends on landing E (Apprehend) to drag you into his Q (Decimate) radius and start stacking Hemorrhage. Block that one ability with W (Riposte) and the fight inverts completely — you get a free stun and a damage window instead of eating his combo. The overall shape reads as even because Fiora's mid-game item spike (Ravenous Hydra into Death's Dance) closes the gap Darius opens in the first six levels.

theirWindow.when: E (Apprehend) is up and you're pushed
theirWindow.what: He pulls you in, follows with Q (Decimate) plus autos to stack Hemorrhage, then threatens R (Noxian Guillotine) once you're below the execute line. Don't stand and trade unless you can immediately parry — back off or force him to waste E on a minion wave first.

yourWindow.what: He has no way to stop you disengaging, so this is when you initiate. Land Q (Lunge) to proc your passive vitals for bonus true damage and healing, then walk away before E comes back up.

start.why: The standard start in 89.2% of games (46.8% WR over 547 games) — the extra sustain and damage let you match Darius's early poke instead of losing every auto-for-auto trade outright.

boots.why: Run in 76% of games (49.1% WR over 428 games) because Darius's damage is almost entirely auto-attacks and Q (Decimate) physical hits — the flat reduction blunts his all-in far more than magic resist does.

core.why: First item in the most-played and highest-WR path (55.2% over 125 games, 37.9% pick) — the sustain from the active heal directly answers Darius's sustained trading pattern.
Second item in that same path — the attack speed and burst proc give you the tempo to actually punish him when E (Apprehend) is down.
Closes the top build path — the damage-over-time conversion is critical against a champion whose whole kit is built around burst true damage from stacked Hemorrhage.

situational.when: you're ahead and want a faster all-in burst instead of the hydra-into-trinity sustain path (56.5% WR over 46 games taking hydra into eclipse into death's dance)
you're already snowballing hard and want to close games faster (71.9% WR over 32 games on the hydra-eclipse-endless hunger path, though the sample is small)
the enemy team stacks hard CC or AP burn beyond just Darius (38.6% WR over 70 games, still a real pick at 12.4%)
you expect to be poked out or all-inned before level 3 rather than trading evenly (64.5% WR over 31 games, though a much smaller sample than the blade start)

runes.keystoneWhy: The guaranteed burst on the third hit rewards landing a clean auto-weave trade window right after you parry his E — you want that burst concentrated on him specifically, a single isolated target, not spread across a prolonged fight.

summoners.why: Run in 92% of games at 48% WR. Ignite is explicitly what closes the gap in this matchup — it lets you punish Darius the moment he overextends without E (Apprehend) up, since he has no self-sustain to out-heal the burn once you commit.

playing.title: Save W for his E, not his Q
playing.detail: Riposte parries a single instance of damage or CC — spending it on his E (Apprehend) fully negates the pull that sets up his whole combo and stuns him for a free follow-up. Don't waste it blocking a Q poke when he still has E in the bank.

playing.title: Stand near minions during his Q
playing.detail: Decimate deals less damage per target the more units it hits, so staying near your wave when he winds it up costs him a large chunk of his poke damage compared to being his sole target.

playing.title: Count Hemorrhage stacks before extending
playing.detail: Five stacks of his passive add bonus true damage and set up a much scarier Noxian Guillotine. If you're already stacked up and below half health, disengage rather than trade again — that's exactly the state his execute wants you in.

playing.title: Trade only with vitals procs available
playing.detail: Land Q (Lunge) to trigger your passive's vital-point bonus true damage and healing before committing to extended exchanges — it's your only built-in sustain in lane before Ravenous Hydra comes online.

playing.title: Bait E before short-trading
playing.detail: Threaten a trade from just outside his E range to force it out on a whiff or on a minion, then punish the 16-20 second cooldown window with a real engage.

playing.title: Delay all-ins until items land
playing.detail: Given the lane and solo-kill deficit, avoid forcing extended fights before level 9-11; let Ravenous Hydra's sustain and Trinity Force's tempo bring the matchup back to even before you start initiating instead of reacting.

playing.title: Use R to end fights, not start them
playing.detail: Grand Challenge's true damage and healing are best spent finishing a trade you already won with Q and W procs, since it ignores the resistances he stacks and secures kills your Death's Dance damage-over-time would otherwise let him survive.

brief.patchCaveat: Win rates, pick rates, sample sizes, item paths, runes, and summoner spells above are measured OP.GG data from real games on the current patch — treat those numbers as fact. The mechanical reasoning, timing windows, and trade patterns explaining why those numbers look the way they do are my own tactical read, not measured data.

stats.opponentTip: Bring Ignite to pressure Darius in lane. Always use [W] to block his (E).
